english.title: Arson
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) committed arson in that without lawful excuse you

(A)_[destroyed]_
(B)_[damaged]_

by fire **(..SPECIFY THE PROPERTY..)

(C)_[to the value of **(..SPECIFY THE VALUE..)]_
(D)_[of a value unknown]_

belonging to **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1), 1(3) and 4 of the Criminal Damage Act 1971.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
committed arson in that without lawful excuse
destroy / damage by fire
property with intent to destroy / damage it or
being recklessly as to whether
such property was destroyed / damaged

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Property damaged/destroyed must not belong to defendant(s).
(ii) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where the damage is to a spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iii) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Life imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
